title: feat(plugin-list)!: a chart list view binds only an ADR-0021 dataset; the legacy chart binding retires on every route (objectui#6152, round 15)
body:
Fixes #6152
Clause-②: no

Round 15 of objectui#6152: class D of the round-13 census (the legacy chart binding), plus the two items round 14's ACCEPT (`6079839306`, item 3) carried here. Claim `6080177854`; rulings `6077535247` (Q1 → C, Q2 → A). Base: `main` at `3fd8625`. Every gate below was read at head `48f102b`.

## What changes

**A chart list view binds only an ADR-0021 `dataset`, on every route.** The pre-ADR-0021 inline axes (`xAxisField` / `categoryField`, `yAxisFields` / `valueField`, `aggregation`) are refused by name at every door: the spec's `ListChartConfigSchema` is a strict object of `chartType` / `dataset` / `dimensions` / `values`, and the `options` bag is that block's own partial. Three routes still read them and drew an inline aggregate, floored at `'name'` / `'value'` when the block declared nothing. All three are retired:

- `@object-ui/plugin-list`, `ListView.tsx`: `resolveListChartBinding` loses its legacy leg. `ListChartBinding` loses `categoryField` / `valueField`, and its `shape` is `'dataset' | 'unbound'`. The capability gate asks the same resolver, so it no longer offers Chart for a legacy block. `case 'chart'` loses the legacy return and its floors. A block that names no `dataset` builds the UNBOUND node: `{ type: 'object-chart', objectName, chartType, filter }`.
- `@object-ui/app-shell`, `views/ObjectView.tsx`: the object page's own chart branch in `renderListView` is retired too. It read `xAxisField`, `yAxisFields[0]`, `aggregation`, and `series` / `filter` off the block. The census did not list it as a reader (H1 below). It now builds the same unbound node, without a filter.
- `@object-ui/plugin-view`, `ObjectView.tsx`: the same retirement in `generateViewSchema`'s `case 'chart'`.

`ObjectChart` refuses the unbound node on screen with its objectui#8168 screen (`chart-missing-category-axis`, `role="alert"`). It no longer aggregates on a name nobody wrote.

**Carried from round 14 (ACCEPT item 3):**

- plugin-view's kanban branch stops reading `kanban.conditionalFormatting` (H3 below). The view-level `conditionalFormatting` of the active host `views` entry is the one place the key is read.
- The development-only flat-key warnings in `generateViewSchema` and app-shell's `renderListView` no longer name keys every per-kind block refuses. They used to tell an author to move those keys into the block.
  - plugin-view drops `dateField`, `groupBy`, `groupField`, `imageField` and `subtitleField`.
  - app-shell drops those five plus `xAxisField`, `subjectField`, `endField`, `cardFields`, `yAxisFields`, `aggregation` and `series`.
  - Each remaining key is declared by some spec per-kind block. Each list was checked once against the spec 17.7.0 block shapes; no instrument re-derives it.

**Prose:** comments that said the list-view relays still read the axes were updated in:

- `ListView.tsx`;
- `objectql.zod.ts` and `objectql.ts` (`@object-ui/types`, comments only);
- `ObjectChart.tsx` (`@object-ui/plugin-charts`): the `resolveChartCategoryField` docblock and the 8168 docblock, comments only. The refusal path's code is untouched.
- the headers of the re-judged tests.

The pending `.changeset/6152-list-view-readers-retired.md` and `.changeset/6152-list-view-options-bag.md` each gain an append-only dated note, because their "the legacy chart axes are still read" sentence goes false. The new `.changeset/6152-list-view-legacy-chart-retired.md` declares:

- `minor` for plugin-list, app-shell and plugin-view (breaking for a stored chart view that names no `dataset`);
- `patch` for plugin-charts and types (comments only);
- the FROM → TO table, with production stated as NOT MEASURED.

## Measured before any edit

**H2: what a `chart` view with no dataset renders once the legacy branch is gone.** A scratch probe rendered the real `ListView` and the real `ObjectChart` (deleted afterwards):

- **Doors.** objectui's `ListViewSchema` ACCEPTS `viewType: 'chart'` with no block, and `options: { chart: { chartType } }` with no dataset. The spec's view write door (`VIEW_METADATA_MEMBERS.listOverlay`) ACCEPTS both too. So door-legal views reach this path, besides stored legacy rows.
- **On `main`.** Those views drew an aggregate grouped by `name` that counted `value`: the floors.
- **Three candidate node shapes, through the real `ObjectChart`:**
  1. An object-bound node naming no category gives the 8168 refusal, loud (`role="alert"`). Its remedy reads "Declare one of: aggregate.groupBy, xAxisKey, xAxis.field", which is `ObjectChart`'s vocabulary, not the list view's dataset block.
  2. A node with neither `objectName` nor `dataset` renders blank.
  3. A `case 'chart'` that returns nothing leaves the memo `undefined`, and the render site dereferences `viewComponentSchema.type`: a crash (read from source).

So shape 1 is the only loud answer within this surface. It is what is built. Naming the dataset block on screen would need new release text in every locale pack, which is outside this surface. That is open question Q1 in the report on objectui#6152, with options.

**H3: does any door that feeds plugin-view's kanban branch accept `kanban.conditionalFormatting`?** Each door was read with a control:

- **Refused** (`unrecognized_keys` at the block; each control accepted): the named-view record (the spec's `ViewSchema.listViews`, and objectui's `ObjectViewSchema` / `StrictAnyComponentSchema` / `safeValidateSchema` over it), the spec's authoring `ListViewSchema`, the view write door (`listOverlay`), and objectui's `ListViewSchema` in both nestings.
- **Host `views` entry (`ObjectViewProps['views']`).** It declares no `kanban` member, only `[key: string]: any`. A `tsc` probe compiled `kanban.conditionalFormatting`, the round-14-retired `kanban.groupField` and an arbitrary `kanban.zzz_not_a_key` alike. Its control is the one declared block, `tree`: it refused `parentFeild` (TS2561).
- **Reading.** That entry judges nothing under `kanban`. It admits keys round 14 retired on this same branch, so it does not count as a door that accepts the key. Every door that judges the key refuses it, so the read retires. `ObjectKanbanSchema` does declare `conditionalFormatting`, but that is the `object-kanban` NODE's member, not the list view's block.

## Fixtures re-judged (three dispositions)

| file | disposition |
| :--- | :--- |
| plugin-list `ListView.chart-capability-7544` | Turned: the two "offers Chart for a legacy block" arms now assert it is NOT offered, and a bag arm is added. The two lone-axis arms are kept and renamed. Two render arms are replaced: a legacy block and no block both build the unbound node, with no aggregate and no axis. |
| plugin-list `ListView.searchWithheldTreeChart-10326`, `ListView.datasetChartToolbarFilter-10327`, `ListView.datasetChartAppliedFilter-10512`, `ListView.selfQueryingViewsToolbarState-10250` | Re-spelled: "a chart bound to the list object" was spelled with the legacy axes and is now a `chart` view naming no dataset. The switch case uses the dataset block, the only one the gate offers. |
| app-shell `ObjectView.chartRelay-7823` | Turned: the toggle for a legacy block now reads `false`. The pointer still carries the block whole. |
| app-shell `ObjectView.chartConfigForward-7891` | Turned: the legacy positive control now asserts the unbound node. Added: two unbound arms, plus a describe for the flat-key warning. |
| app-shell `ObjectView.refreshInPlace-10035` | Re-spelled to the dataset block. |
| app-shell `ObjectView.calendarBinding-7029`, `ObjectView.galleryBinding-7547`, `ObjectView.ganttBinding-7070` | Converted, as each case instructs: see the note after this table. |
| plugin-view `ObjectView.kanbanConditionalFormatting` | Turned: the nested rule no longer reaches the node, and the view-level rule is the one read. The header, the failure-message remedy and a stale round-14 note were corrected. |
| plugin-charts `ObjectChart.absentCategoryAxisRefusal-8168` | Replaced: the three relay transcriptions pinned branches this PR deletes. They move to a describe that asserts the refusal FIRES on each relay's unbound node, with a control. |
| plugin-view `ObjectView.namedViewProtocolKeys-8980`, types `object-chart-legacy-axis-keys-retired-10608` | Prose only. |
| new: app-shell `__tests__/listViewLegacyChartRetired-6152` | The real `ListView` and the real `ObjectChart`. Five shapes with no dataset each give the refusal and no aggregate query; the dataset block, as control, is not refused. It lives in app-shell because `plugin-list` does not depend on `plugin-charts`, so `plugin-list`'s type-check refused it (TS2882). |
| new: plugin-view `ObjectView.legacyChartRetired-6152` | The chart branch (three legacy shapes build the unbound node; the dataset block is the control) and the warning (five refused keys are not named; `titleField` is the lit control). |

**Source scans: no fabricated binding floor remains.** The same-class control of the three app-shell source scans was anchored on the chart branch's `|| 'value'` measure floor, and this PR deletes it. No one-rung fabricated binding floor remains in app-shell's `ObjectView.tsx`. What is left floors:

- a display title or label at `'name'`;
- a view `type` at `'grid'`;
- a chart family at `'bar'`.

As instructed, the calendar and gallery cases now assert that NONE remains. Each still has a machinery control on `'name'`. The gantt control moves to that anchor beside the same assertion.

Census candidates left unchanged and still right: `CreateViewDialog.chartBinding-11576` and `ObjectView.createChartView-11576` (the writer writes the dataset block), and `InterfaceListPage.treeChartRelay-11572`.

## Ablations (reverse verification)

Each leg went through objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. That tool carries its own EXIT/INT/TERM trap and proves its restore; a belt trap in the driver restored every path too. Every leg hit its anchor exactly once. After every leg the blob equalled HEAD and `git diff HEAD` was empty for all three source files. No `dist` is involved: the suites resolve these packages to `src` through the vitest aliases.

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A1 | ListView's unbound node grows the `name` / `value` floors back | red | 7 red: five arms in the real-route pin, two in 7544. The dataset control stayed green. |
| A2 | the resolver's legacy `resolves` comes back | red | 6 red: four in 7544, two in 7823. The lone-axis arms stayed green, as predicted. |
| A3 | plugin-view reads `kanban.conditionalFormatting` again | red | 2 red |
| A4 | plugin-view's warning names `groupField` again | red | 1 red |
| A5 | app-shell's unbound node grows an aggregate from the axes | red | 2 red |
| A6 | app-shell's warning names `xAxisField` again | red | 1 red |
| A7 | plugin-view's unbound node grows the floors back | red | 3 red |

## Gates (head `48f102b`)

- **Test battery** (vitest from the repo root, `--maxWorkers=2`, under `os-verify-lock`): 648 files in four chunks. The battery is every test that imports or names `ListView.tsx`, either `ObjectView.tsx`, `ObjectChart.tsx`, `objectql.ts` or `objectql.zod.ts` by relative path, or the `plugin-list` / `plugin-view` / `plugin-charts` package names; every changed test; and the whole `scripts/__tests__` suite. Result: 646 files passed and 2 skipped; 15019 tests passed and 2 skipped. Every chunk printed `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The first run of chunk 0 found the three source-scan controls above red; they were converted and the chunk re-run green at this head.
- **type-check** after building the console's closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...' --concurrency=2`, exit 0): exit 0 at this head for `@object-ui/types`, `plugin-charts`, `plugin-list`, `plugin-view`, `app-shell` and `@object-ui/console`. Each run echoed its `type-check` script.
- **eslint** (`--no-inline-config --format json`) on the 23 changed TS files: 0 errors. The modified files carry 574 warnings at this head, the same 574 as on `main`; the two new test files add 7 `no-explicit-any` warnings (the house harness). The linted population is `eslint.config.js`'s `**/*.{ts,tsx}` globs. Linting is not type-aware (no `parserOptions.project`), so no untouched file's verdict can move. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- **Changeset gates** exit 0: `check-changeset-presence`, `-no-major`, `-fixed`, `-claims`, `-overwrite` (report-only: the two dated notes, declarations unchanged) and `check-pending-changeset-literals`.
- **Eager closure** (H4), console built under the lock: `main` 3,240,183 B gzip; head 3,239,902 B; delta −281 B. Headroom to `MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES` (3,281,467, untouched): 41,565 B. `check-eager-closure-budget` exit 0.
- **Other gates, exit 0:**
  - `check-sdui-registration-pins`;
  - `check-control-bytes`;
  - `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new);
  - `check-vi-mock-specifiers` / `-inherit` / `-override-shape`;
  - `check-test-path-roots`;
  - `check-type-check-coverage` and `check-lint-coverage`;
  - `check-phantom-dependencies`;
  - `check-handler-key-read-sites`;
  - `check-unreferenced-sources`;
  - `check-i18n-call-site-keys`;
  - `check-spec-symbol-derivation`;
  - `check-object-metadata-write-doors`;
  - `check-element-data-source-declaration`;
  - `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (NOT GOVERNED).
- No README or doc page changes, so the doc gates are not owed.

## Acceptance notes

- **Wasted fetch.** On the unbound node, the 8168 screen still lets `ObjectChart` issue one `find` of the object's rows (no `$top`) before it refuses. The probe measured one `find` and no `aggregate`. This PR makes every chart view that names no dataset reach that path. It is in the report on objectui#6152 as a finding and as part of Q1.
- **`UnifiedViewConfig.chart`** in `@object-ui/types` (`designer.ts`) still types the legacy axes. It is exported and has no consumer in this repository. Noted, not filed.
- **The `object-chart` tombstone messages** still describe `xAxisField` / `yAxisFields` / `aggregation` as "the list-view chart block's spelling". That is published refusal text, left unchanged here.
- **The flat-key warnings stay coarse per kind.** They name a key declared by any block (for example `startDateField` on a kanban view) and point at the view's own kind. This predates this PR and is development-only console text.
